speaker: Doctor
text: The imaging findings are classic for Hirschsprung disease, characterized by the transition zone in the distal colon. To definitively confirm the diagnosis, I need to verify the absence of ganglion cells in the bowel wall. REQUEST TEST: Rectal biopsy

speaker: Doctor

The normal biopsy is unexpected given the classic imaging, so let me ask one last question: Has he ever passed meconium within the first 48 hours of life, or has he had episodes of bilious vomiting?

REQUEST TEST: Anorectal manometry

speaker: Doctor
text: The normal biopsy and manometry results effectively rule out Hirschsprung disease despite the suggestive imaging. Given the abdominal distension and feeding difficulties in an infant, I suspect a functional obstruction or malrotation. REQUEST TEST: Abdominal Ultrasound

speaker: Doctor
text: Since structural causes like Hirschsprung disease and malrotation have been ruled out, I need to consider metabolic or functional issues. Has he experienced any episodes of lethargy, vomiting, or failure to thrive since birth? REQUEST TEST: Sweat Chloride Test

speaker: Doctor
text: With Hirschsprung, malrotation, and cystic fibrosis ruled out, I need to investigate potential food protein-induced enterocolitis or eosinophilic gastroenteritis. Has he been exclusively breastfed or formula-fed, and have you noticed any rash, eczema, or blood in his stool? REQUEST TEST: Stool Calprotectin

speaker: Doctor
text:
With inflammatory markers and common structural causes ruled out, I am concerned about an intestinal motility disorder like chronic intestinal pseudo-obstruction. Does the baby have any known neurological issues, or has he ever required nasogastric tube feeding due to severe vomiting?
